name: msgspec-serde
workload: Encoding/decoding msgspec.Struct models (including NumPy-array fields) generated from FlatBuffers .fbs IDL, plus a 1,000-object recursive File/Directory graph benchmark at 16- and 256-value vector lengths
claimed_speedup: ~20-22x faster to encode and ~11-13x faster to materialize (full decode) vs the official Python FlatBuffers API; selected-field access ~1.2x faster; full traversal 1.5-2.9x faster (verbatim from benchmarks.md)
compiler_and_flags: N/A (Python); CPython 3.13.5, msgspec 0.21.1, NumPy 2.5.2, Python FlatBuffers 25.12.19, flatc 23.5.2, msgspec-serde 0.1.0
hardware: Intel Core i7-8650U CPU, single isolated core, Linux
tradeoffs: Python-only; the speedup is specific to msgspec-serde's generated Struct/View codec path vs the stock Python flatbuffers package's Object API, not a change to the FlatBuffers wire format itself; at 256-value vectors the plain FlatBuffers decode path is fastest overall, not msgspec-serde; requires flatc for IDL codegen
caveats: Baseline is the official Python FlatBuffers binding (interpreted-language overhead), not FlatBuffers' native C++ core, so the win largely reflects Python API overhead rather than a beat of FlatBuffers' underlying engine; single machine/CPU model; project is brand new (1 star, days old) though methodology and reproduction commands are fully documented
found_via: Hacker News: query 'faster than flatbuffers' -> 'Show HN: msgspec-serde, Fast serialization for msgspec, flatbuffers, & arrays' (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49698621)

name: Imprint
workload: Merging (composing) and projecting (field-subset reading) two records of increasing size, comparing Imprint's offset-directory composition/projection against protobuf decode+re-encode
claimed_speedup: up to 76% faster than protobuf when merging two records, with Imprint running in near-constant time versus protobuf's linear degradation as record size grows; projection benchmarked similarly (chart shows Imprint flat, protobuf degrading linearly) but no single numeric ratio is given for projection in the text
tradeoffs: Field directory adds roughly 3-5 bytes/field of overhead versus protobuf's ~1-varint tag/field, so wire size is slightly larger; schema-less reads require scanning a directory; optimized for compose/project (stream-join) access patterns rather than raw sequential encode/decode throughput
caveats: README shows only chart images plus one headline percentage; compiler flags, CPU model, and the exact protobuf implementation/version compared are not stated, so this falls short of a reproducible Tier A result even though the Criterion-style benchmark code (benches/serde_bench.rs) is public; last commit over a year old
found_via: Hacker News: query 'Show HN serialization' -> 'Show HN: Imprint – Serialization Format for Data Pipelines' (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44239507)

name: JSBT (@cheprasov/jsbt)
workload: Serializing 10,000 similar/repetitive JavaScript objects (financial/logging-style data with shared structure) and comparing on-wire size across JSON, Protobuf, MsgPack, CBOR, and JSBT
claimed_speedup: JSBT output is about 48x smaller than Protobuf (64,175 bytes vs 3,108,000 bytes) on a 10,000-object repetitive dataset, via structural deduplication and graph references (verbatim numbers from README benchmarks table)
tradeoffs: JSBT is markedly SLOWER per-operation than Protobuf on simple flat objects (31.51 microseconds/op encode vs Protobuf's 3.29 microseconds/op in the project's own table); the size win only materializes for highly repetitive/graph-shaped data; JS/TS runtime-only, not cross-language like Protobuf
caveats: Author states the benchmarks are 'synthetic and indicative, not absolute'; no hardware or compiler/runtime version details given beyond 'Node.js'; the win is specifically a compactness (memory) win, not a speed win -- on the same tables JSBT is several times slower in raw encode/decode throughput than Protobuf
